To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
most human cancers express antigens that react in vivo with the humoral antibody of the autologous hosts to fix complement.
the mixed hemadsorption tests demonstrated antibody and complement bound to the cell membrane of human cancer cells in vivo.
the MHA techniques demonstrated antibody and C3 fixed in vivo to human cancer cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of antibody and complement fixed on the membrane of human cancer cells in vivo.
the in vitro detection of antibodies and complement complexed on the cell surface of human cancer.
the in vivo immunobiologic reactions of cancer cells and their relationship to the immunologic status of patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MHA techniques are a sensitive and reliable method for detecting antibody and complement complex on the surface of human cancers in vitro.
the mixed hemadsorption technique is an excellent method for the demonstration of antibody and complement fixed on the surface of human cancers.
the MHA technique is an effective method of demonstrating antibody and complement fixed on the surface of human tumor cells in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cancer is a disease of the immune system, and that the immune system is the most important factor in the control and regulation of cancer.
cancer is antigenic and the immune response to it may be a major factor in determining the outcome of the host's disease.
the MHA techniques can detect in vivo the presence of antibody and C3 complexed on the cell surface of human cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cancer cells are antigenic in vivo and that the immune system of cancer patients can produce antibody that can be detected on the cell surface.
the MHA techniques are simple and sensitive methods for detection of antibody and complement fixed on cell membranes in vitro and that these methods may be useful in studies of human tumors.
the majority of human cancers are antigenically distinct and are recognized as foreign by the immune system of the autologous patient.
